title: Let Party Names No More
description: Let Party Names No More in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Benjamin Beddome wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 396 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christian Unity”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Let par-ty names no more The Chris-tian world o'er-spread; Gen-tile and Jew, and bond and free, Are one in Christ their head.

lines: Gentile and Jew, and bond and free,
Are one in Christ their head.
Those should in holy friendship dwell,
Where streams of pleasure always flow,

licence: Public domain: Benjamin Beddome died in 1795.
credits: Words by Benjamin Beddome (1717–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
